In this petition, the petitioner is seeking grant of bail in Crime No.39/2023 of Kolar women Police,
for the offence punishable under Sections 498(A), 504 & 506 of Ipc and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry

2. Heard the arguments of Sri. Raghavendra S.H learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt.Sowmya R. learned HCGP.
3.
The brief facts of the case are, the marriage of the complainant was solemnised with petitioner on 05.03.2021.
Accused No.2 is the father; accused No.3 is the mother; and accused No.4 is the sister of the petitioner.

Due to miscommunication among themselves, an allegation started against the petitioner and his family members that they have subjected the complainant to harassment in demand of gold and cash as additional NC: 2023:KHC:37720 dowry.
There is an allegation that the complainant encountered the COVID infection during Goa tour on 18.04.2021, she was not provided medical aid by her husband.
Thereafter, differences started between the husband and wife, and it is alleged that the petitioner, his family called her as a patient women, and she was subjected to harassment.
4. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that after the marriage there was a COVID spread.
The complainant was infected with the COVID infection, and she was provided with treatment.
During the period of COVID, everybody was scared, and the complainant expected that the petitioner attend personally, and she also insisted that her husband live separately.
When it was not agreed upon, the complainant introduced the allegation of harassment and dowry.
The accused Nos.2 to 4 were already granted bail by the Court of Sessions.

The petitioner is ready to assist in the NC: 2023:KHC:37720 investigation, having regard to the age of both and to sustain the marital life,
grant of bail is necessary.
5.
Learned HCGP, while opposing the bail application, contended that the petitioner, being the husband, had not discharged his duty when his wife was infected with COVID.

Even after recovery,
she was branded as a patient, and there was a demand for additional dowry, resulting in the complaint.
If bail is granted, the petitioner will repeat the offense, and discretion shall not be exercised in his favour.
Hence, prayed for rejection of bail.
6. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments of both sides and perused the materials on record.
7. There is no dispute that the marriage between the petitioner and the complainant took place on 05.03.2021.
Thereafter, they lived in a matrimonial home.
Even they went to Goa on 18.04.2021.
Unfortunately, the complainant is infected with COVID.

sentences.text: From 18.04.2021 till 28.08.2022, there is no report as to the harassment and demand for dowry.
The complaint was filed on 01.09.2023 one year after the alleged incident.
Both the petitioner and the complainant are at the initial stage of their marriage, differences of opinion and misunderstandings are common, they are quarreling with each other.
The trivial dispute between the husband and wife will damage their marital life.
Since accused Nos.2 to 4 were already granted bail by the court of Sessions, I do not find any reasons to refuse exercise of discretion in favour of the petitioner.
In order to restore their matrimonial life exercise of discretion is necessary.
The petitioner has undertaken to abide any conditions that would be imposed by this court.
Conditions will meet the apprehension of the prosecution.
Hence petition merits consideration.

8. In the result, the following;
NC: 2023:KHC:37720 ORDER
( i) The Petition is allowed.

(ii) The petitioner is ordered to be released on bail in the event of his arrest in Crime No.39/2023 registered by the Kolar Women Police, for the offence punishable under Sections 498(A), 504 & 506 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, on execution of a personal bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with one surety for the like-sum to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer.
